NutsSync, Copyright 2026 Evan Bolton, LGPL-2.1-or-later.
Source: https://www.nutsdeveloping.com/source/ (NutsEmu build 1521).
The exact archive and original header digest are recorded in source-origin.json.
COPYING.LIB contains the license. Source and relinking build scripts are shipped
in the Madeira source repository; the native library is statically linked.

Madeira modifications, 2026-10-18:
- Reserve the zero object slot encoding and capture numbers before unlocking.
- Use 11 generation bits for Madeira's existing pseudo-descriptor ABI; retire
  slots before generation wrap, preventing stale descriptor reuse.
- Add object allocation and waiter lifecycle callbacks for descriptor references
  and cleanup on native thread termination, including already-signaled waiters.
- Pin alert objects with the same waiter lifetime as other objects.
- Use os_unfair_lock with ownership and priority donation in Madeira's single
  native host task, retaining NutsSync's word-based blocking waiter protocol.
- Use private compare-and-wait operations in that host and no periodic timer
  for infinite waits; atomic state checks preserve wake-before-park ordering.
- Integrate through build/madsync/nutssync_adapter.c and madsync_bridge.c,
  preserving Wine object/access/APC protocols and legacy synchronization choices.
- Coordinate persistent Mach suspension with the synchronization lock so a
  thread cannot be frozen while holding that lock.

Madeira yield-policy adaptation, 2026-10-19:
- Apply Wine patch 0122's 2 ms elapsed budget and 100 us continuity gap to
  NtYieldExecution. Retain Madeira's non-depressing Mach handoff and 100 us
  long-poll sleep rather than increasing its periodic wake rate.
- Timestamp after an intentional sleep, initialize shared options once,
  bound overrides, and saturate the optional legacy count.
- Source: the same build-1521 archive (also covering build 1522),
  patches/wine/0122-spin-waits-sleep-only-after-2-ms.patch.
